scope: Explicit opt-in ordinary Codex exec/resume native-final transport, preserving one native session per instance. Never substitute app-server, host mode, or a fresh session for this path.

installedVersionEvidence.method: Read-only filesystem symlink resolution; no version command or fresh CLI execution
installedVersionEvidence.limitation: The path identifies the installation inspected, not a fresh executable digest or current native event conformance result. Revalidate executable identity before implementation acceptance.

historicalEvidence.finding: Exec stdout alone does not expose native turn identity or distinguish final_answer from commentary. A final-looking agent_message or exit zero is insufficient.
historicalEvidence.existingProof: validateExecTerminal cross-checks complete current-launch exec JSONL, a fresh output-last-message file, and current rollout suffix containing matching task_started, turn_context, assistant final_answer and task_complete. This is historical prototype proof, not product integration acceptance.
historicalEvidence.publicationLimitation: The historical prototype uses a private Worker messages/post bridge; it is not evidence that ordinary exec already uses the production final-output transaction slot.

currentSourceEvidence.finding: Registered Codex implementation is codex-app-server/v1; there is no ordinary exec adapter. Generic process construction does not add Codex session continuity or native-final proof.
Codex base launch arguments select app-server. Reuse isolation and memory policy deliberately, not this transport default.
RuntimeProfileManifestV3 adapter kind enum includes codex-app-server/v1 but no explicit codex-exec kind.

Both direct and supervised close release the activation environment before activity.finish. recover returns supervisor terminal status without reconstructing a final-output candidate or publication disposition.
Runtime kind mapping and warm admission distinguish known provider adapters; an exec path needs explicit Codex configuration ownership without warm app-server selection.

proposedOwnerPatches.change: Add an explicit codex-exec/v1 runtime adapter kind bound to the codex-cli/v1 catalog probe. Do not add Room business commands or silently reinterpret existing app-server profiles.

proposedOwnerPatches.owner: AgentHost provider driver and native evidence
proposedOwnerPatches.change: Launch ordinary exec/resume with explicit model/effort and existing isolation policy. Freeze launch, session expectation, output file and rollout boundary. Collect native final evidence and usage; emit proof to Host, never mutate Room state in the driver. Disable provider automatic memory on every launch; preserve normal session history.

proposedOwnerPatches.owner: AgentHost runtime composition and session continuity
proposedOwnerPatches.change: Register the explicit exec adapter, reuse ProviderSessionStore, original Worker lease and Host-bodied wake. Existing instances must not silently change transport or replace their native session. Missing required continuity fails closed.

Add a scoped native-final settlement path: drain proof and pending lifecycle writes, submit once through WorkerFinalOutput while original authority is live, then release environment and return actual RunExit plus publication receipt. Keep non-opted-in behavior unchanged; test direct and supervised cleanup separately.
Map explicit exec runtime to existing Codex settings, credentials and standing prompt. Do not route it into the warm app-server adapter. Initially leave selection opt-in.

Reuse existing final-output endpoint, trusted submission slot, freshness check and ACK rules; no new queue, cursor or Task owner. Assert existing action_required handling for invalid, held, rejected and unknown receipts.

prototypeHardeningRequired: Replace line-count rollout suffix selection with an exact path, byte offset and verified unchanged prefix hash; reject truncated, replaced or historical evidence.
Validate model and effort against the frozen runtime binding instead of the prototype's hard-coded gpt-6-luna/low.

On first launch, bind unique launch and output-file identities before spawn. Bind native session once proven by current thread.started and matching session metadata; never find authority by newest file or wall-clock window.

Require unique matching native turn, final phase, message identity, task completion and output file, plus complete error-free exec stream and normal exit; ambiguous or missing proof yields an explicit nonpublished receipt.
Do not use bounded diagnostic stdout as an implicitly complete authority buffer. Track truncation and reject incomplete evidence; use bounded provider-specific parsing.
Use unique per-response usage from current native evidence. Resume turn.completed usage may be cumulative and must not be summed as per-turn usage.
Provider rollout remains diagnostic evidence for explicit opted-in final transport; it never reconstructs Room history, Task completion or delivery ACK.
requiredLifecycleOrdering: Freeze supported transport selection and original Run credential/delivery binding before launch.
Prove native completion and drain session-binding, delivery and usage writes.
Publish at most once with the original execution authority through WorkerFinalOutput.
Preserve receipt, release credentials and resources, and return actual runtime exit independently from business disposition.
On Host crash or lost reply, verify existing durable marker where supported; absent or unavailable proof requires visible action_required, never blind resend or automatic replacement model turn.

newCollectorNegatives: changed prefix, replaced file, historical replay or truncated JSONL
pending tool, error, length termination or abnormal process exit
transport mode off or unsupported target selection
lifecycle: Original Worker credential remains valid until submission settles and is then released on success, held, unknown, rejected and cancellation.
Direct and supervised paths retain actual exit provenance and cleanup on spawn failure and crash.
Publication committed but response lost does not duplicate a message or initiate a replacement model turn.
Crash before publication, missing proof and revoked credentials fail closed instead of degrading to ordinary auto-retry.
Tool-first and native-final-first share the existing dedicated final submission fence.
testPlan.freeRealCLIIntegration: After deterministic red/green tests, run installed ordinary Codex CLI against a local fake provider for two turns of one native session, including a real file tool. Verify exec arguments, memory-off every launch, native evidence, one final-output marker per turn, no model-side posting tool and no post-publication model request. This free run has not been launched by this planning task.

explicitLimits: No source implementation, new tests, CLI launch, deployment or cost acceptance in this task; only this plan artifact is written.
Busy steering and multi-target correctness are separate slices. Do not pretend ordinary exec has app-server steering; unsupported busy delivery retains existing durable follow-up behavior.
Existing Codex app-server collectors and tests are not exec compatibility evidence.
Initial first-session native IDs are generated by the CLI, not known before spawn; prelaunch binding and post-start identity proof must remain distinct claims.
A same-UID full-access CLI is not cryptographically isolated from local diagnostic files. This plan does not claim stronger isolation.
One free fake-model trajectory proves transport behavior only, not model compliance, long-task quality, multi-model performance or economic viability.
